documents.title: User stories — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR
documents.body:
# User stories — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR

## Personas

- **The spec owner** — SPEC §5.7 sets Leptos CSR as the prior and admits SSR only on a measured TTI above 2 s or an auth forcing condition, so the choice must rest on numbers.
- **The S12 UI builder** — builds `apps/web` and consumes the ADR's stack, bundle size, SSE client shape and performance targets.
- **The S2 skeleton implementers** — own the workspace, tenancy and auth; S2/D13 replaces the fixture OP with the real Keycloak `conveyor` realm.
- **The delivery coordinator** — closes tranche 0 and needs one recorded decision with the numbers that produced it.
- **The future maintainer** — reads the Measured table and the revisit triggers when a later Leptos release or a new screen questions the choice.

## Stories

- As the spec owner, I want the CSR prior tested by measurement on both hard screens, so that SPEC §5.7 is confirmed or overridden with evidence rather than opinion.
- As the S12 builder, I want one recorded stack decision, so that `apps/web` is not relitigated screen by screen.
- As the S12 builder, I want the measured TTI, bundle, first-render, drag and cold-build numbers, so that the size budget and performance targets are set from evidence.
- As the S2 implementers, I want the auth flow proven per stack, so that the real Keycloak integration starts from a known flow shape and a known cost.
- As the delivery coordinator, I want the spike deleted and the ADR kept, so that tranche 0 closes with one durable artefact and no dead code.
- As a future maintainer, I want explicit revisit triggers, so that the decision is reopened on evidence instead of drifting.

## Scenarios

- Given SPEC §5.7's rule, when both stacks were measured on the board, then interaction TTI at 4× CPU / Slow 4G was CSR 5426 ms (5408–5628) vs SSR 5736 ms (5705–5758), n=5, non-overlapping — SSR did not beat CSR on TTI.
- Given the same rule, when CSR auth-code + PKCE was exercised, then 3/3 login → board → logout cycles passed with the token in memory and a gated deep link — auth did not force cookies, so SSR lost on both required counts and CSR was chosen.
- Given the two stacks share one component tree, when the SSR board was loaded, then exactly one board fetch per page load was counted in 5/5 runs — the hydration double-fetch trap did not reproduce on Leptos 0.9.0-rc1.
- Given 500 cards in 10 lists, when first render was measured all-at-once, then SSR reached 1444 ms (945 ms virtualised) vs CSR 4726 ms (4726 ms) — SSR's paint win did not survive to interactivity.
- Given the §7 drag threshold of at least 95 % of frames at or under 16.7 ms, when the 2 s drag ran, then neither stack met it (CSR 80.0 %, SSR 76.5 %, 0 long tasks over 50 ms on both) — symmetric, so not a stack signal.
- Given the finished spike, when the ADR absorbed `RESULTS.md`, then the spike was deleted and `apps/web` was still absent.

## Verify

- `test -f docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` and `grep -q '^## Decision' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` — the ADR exists with its decision.
- `grep -cE '^\| *[1-8] ' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` — prints 16, the 8 metrics × 2 stacks.
- `grep -qE '^## (Measured|Consequences)' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` — both sections present.
- `find . -path '*spikes*'` — prints nothing.
- `lsof -nP -iTCP:8791 -iTCP:8801 -iTCP:8802 -sTCP:LISTEN` — prints nothing.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store seed_programme` — S01 is a tranche-0 project, `status: closed`, `measured_status: built`, `issues: []`.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/slices/S01-ui-spike.md` §1, §5, §7.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` — Accepted 2026-11-08.
- Consumers: S12 (`apps/web`), S2/D13 (the real Keycloak realm).

## Notes

Reconstructed for standard v4 on 2026-11-28 from the plan, the ADR and the register. S01 carries no issue and no PR; the plan is its build record.

documents.title: Acceptance criteria — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR

## Scenarios

- The decision is CSR, and it cites the measured numbers: interaction TTI CSR 5426 ms vs SSR 5736 ms, with auth passing on both stacks and no forcing condition.
- Both hard screens were built twice — board and chat, CSR and SSR — from one shared component tree against one fixture.
- The fixture is deterministic and DB-free: 500 cards in 10 lists, `card.moved` SSE every 2 s with monotonic `id:`, a 50-message history, 80 tokens then `tool_call` then `done`, and `/health` returning `ok`.
- The decision-bearing metrics carry n=5 per stack — TTI, bundle, 500-card first render, drag frames — and auth carries 3/3 per stack.
- The hydration double-fetch question is answered with a count: exactly 1 board fetch per page load, 5/5 runs, including with the client fallback disabled.
- The drag threshold outcome is recorded without softening: at least 95 % of frames at or under 16.7 ms was not met by CSR (80.0 %) or SSR (76.5 %), with 0 long tasks over 50 ms on both.
- The unmeasured rows are declared: metric 5 SSR and metric 6 on both stacks were skipped inside the coordinator time-box; metric 5 CSR is a single run, p50 1.0 ms and p95 1.8 ms over 30 events.
- The ADR carries 16 measured rows (8 metrics × 2 stacks), `## Decision`, `## Consequences` and revisit triggers.
- The spike is deleted with no trace, and `apps/web` was left unpopulated for S12.
- No spike port (8791, 8801, 8802) is left listening.

## Verify commands

- `grep -cE '^\| *[1-8] ' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` → 16.
- `grep -q '^## Decision' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` and `grep -qE '^## (Measured|Consequences)' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` → both true.
- `find . -path '*spikes*' | wc -l` → 0.
- `lsof -nP -iTCP:8791 -iTCP:8801 -iTCP:8802 -sTCP:LISTEN` → empty.
- With the fixture up: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8791/api/boards/demo` → 500 cards; `curl -sN 'http://127.0.0.1:8791/api/events?board=demo'` → `id:` 2 s apart; `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8791/health` → `ok`. These were recorded before deletion.
- `npx -y lighthouse@12 http://127.0.0.1:8801/ --only-categories=performance --throttling-method=simulate --throttling.cpuSlowdownMultiplier=4 --throttling.requestLatencyMs=150 --throttling.downloadThroughputKbps=1638.4 --throttling.uploadThroughputKbps=675 --output=json --output-path=/tmp/s1-csr-lh-1.json --chrome-flags='--headless=new'` — run 1 of 5; runs 2–5 write `/tmp/s1-csr-lh-2.json` to `-5.json`, and the same command targets `:8802` for SSR.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store seed_programme` — the register row.

## Results

Met on a gate that carried a decision. CSR was chosen: SSR lost on interaction TTI (5736 vs 5426 ms, non-overlapping ranges, about 5.7 % slower) and did not force cookie-based auth (both stacks passed 3/3), and the rule makes a loss on both a CSR decision. SSR's first-paint win was real — 1444 ms vs 4726 ms for 500 cards — but did not survive to interactivity, and the known hydration double-fetch trap did not reproduce (1 fetch per page load, 5/5). Bundle: CSR 290723 bytes gzip-9 (809797 raw) vs SSR 301017 (844826). Cold build: CSR 44.41 s (35.58–54.71) vs SSR 56.54 s and 79.95 s (n=2). Drag: both missed the 95 % frame target (80.0 % / 76.5 %), with 0 long tasks over 50 ms. Unmeasured and declared in the ADR: metric 5 SSR, metric 6 on both stacks; metric 5 CSR is n=1.

## Status

met — the ADR is Accepted (2026-11-08), the gate's 16 rows and required sections are present, the spike is deleted and S01 reads closed and built. The two unmeasured rows and the missed drag threshold are recorded in the ADR, not waived; neither changes the stack decision.

## Links

- Plan §7 (gate), §8 (traps), §9 (decisions closed here); ADR `docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md`.

documents.title: Definition of ready — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR
documents.body:
# Definition of ready — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR

## Independent

The spike is throwaway and file-disjoint from the workspace: `spikes/web` carries its own empty `[workspace]` table and is never a member, and `apps/web`, `crates/*` and the workspace root are untouched. S01 has no incoming dependency (`depends_on: []`); its consumers are downstream — S12 for the UI build and S2/D13 for the real Keycloak realm.

## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed: one recorded CSR-versus-SSR decision carrying the measured numbers, per SPEC §5.7 and the §8 S1 gate. The mechanics were the negotiable part and were settled by the plan: which two screens, the fixture's four routes, all-at-once as the decision configuration with virtualised as a sub-row, and auth as a pass or forcing condition rather than a latency race.

## Valuable

It removes the named risk that S12 builds `apps/web` on the wrong stack or relitigates the choice per screen. It also prices the decision: the authenticated SSE shim, the 790 KiB raw / 291 kB gzip-9 bundle, the re-login on reload, and the server binary and CSRF surface that CSR avoids.

## Estimable

The plan names every file, command and port, and every build step is at most one day (14 steps). The measurement is bounded: 8 metrics × 2 stacks, five runs for the decision-bearing rows, median with min–max, and one fixture reused per run.

## Small

One slice, one decision, one fixture and two packages. There is no issue and no PR — the plan is the build record — and the deliverable shrinks to one ADR at the end because the spike is deleted.

## Testable

The §7 gate is executable and all-must-be-true: 16 measured rows, `## Decision`, `## Consequences`, no `spikes` path, `apps/web` absent, and no listening port on 8791, 8801 or 8802. Every metric row names the command that produced it, so any number is re-derivable while the spike exists.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: none — `depends_on: []`.
- blocks: nothing formally; S12 consumes the ADR before building `apps/web`.
- related: SPEC §5.7 (the prior and the forcing conditions), SPEC §8 S1 (the gate), CONTRACT §11 (the ADR is the only durable artefact).
- consumed by: the S2/D13 Keycloak work, which inherits the fixture OP's flow shape and the SSE shim cost.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/slices/S01-ui-spike.md` §2, §3, §7.

documents.title: Definition of done — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR
documents.body:
# Definition of done — UI spike — Leptos CSR vs Leptos SSR

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Verify |
|---|---|
| CSR vs SSR decided on the measured numbers | 16 rows in the ADR's Measured table (`grep -cE '^\| *[1-8] ' docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` prints 16) and a Decision naming TTI 5426 vs 5736 ms |
| Both screens built twice from one component tree | board and chat each served and measured on `:8801` (CSR) and `:8802` (SSR), from one shared `spikes/web/shared/ui.rs` |
| Fixture deterministic and DB-free | 500 cards in 10 lists; `card.moved` every 2 s with monotonic `id:`; 50-message history; 80 tokens then `tool_call` then `done`; `/health` returns `ok` |
| Auth proven per stack | `node /tmp/s1-tools/auth.js http://127.0.0.1:8801 3` and the same on `:8802` — 3/3 each; CSR token in memory, SSR HttpOnly `s1_session` plus CSRF |
| The decision's costs named | ADR Consequences: SSE shim, bundle 790 KiB raw and 291 kB gzip-9, re-login on reload, no server binary |
| Spike deleted, ADR kept | `test ! -e spikes`; `find . -path '*spikes*'` prints nothing; `test -f docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` |
| `apps/web` unpopulated by S01 | `test ! -e apps/web` at closure; S12 populated it later |
| Ports released | `lsof -nP -iTCP:8791 -iTCP:8801 -iTCP:8802 -sTCP:LISTEN` prints nothing |

## Evidence at completion

`docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md` — Status Accepted, 2026-11-08 — carries the 8 × 2 Measured table with the command per row, the Decision (CSR), Consequences and Revisit triggers. The register carries S01 as tranche 0, `status: closed`, `measured_status: built`, `issues: []`. The spike and its `RESULTS.md` were deleted after the ADR absorbed their table (S1-D1, CONTRACT §11). Metrics 5 (SSR) and 6 (both) were not measured, and metric 4 missed its threshold on both stacks; all three are stated in the ADR.

## Repo gate

The plan §7 executable block was the gate and every condition held: 16 rows, `## Decision`, `## Consequences`, no spike, `apps/web` absent, ports free, no `spikes` trace. S01 landed no PR, and its Rust was throwaway and deleted, so no continuous compile gate covers it; the repository's preflight and PR CI remain the standing gate for what survives, which is documentation.

## Merge and closure

There was no unit issue, branch or PR — the plan is the build record and the slice closed at tranche 0 on the executable gate. Closure is the decision itself: one ADR, one stack, the spike gone and `apps/web` left to S12. The revisit triggers in the ADR are how the decision comes back, not a re-plan.

## Links

- Plan §7, §8, §9, §10; ADR `docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md`.
